column1: # Hausa (ha) catalog. Columns, separated by a TAB:  context <TAB> source <TAB> translation
#   context  empty                a plain UI string; `source` is the English text in the code
#            @id                  a command id (e.g. file.saveAs): wins over the English text for
#                                 that menu item, so one id can read differently from its twin
#                                 the language's forms separated by "|" (see `plural` in i18n/mod.rs)
#            anything else        a disambiguating context passed to `tr_ctx`
#   escapes  \n  \t  \\  inside a column. `{name}` placeholders must appear in both columns.
#   lines starting with # and blank lines are ignored.
# Clean-room: every entry was written from the plain meaning of the English label in standard
# (Kano-based) Hausa in Boko orthography, with the hooked letters ɓ ɗ ƙ ƴ and ʼ, using ordinary
# Hausa words where they read naturally (ajiye, buɗe, soke, share, launi, girma, burushi, tasha,
# hanya ...) and established loanwords where Hausa speakers use them (fayil, pikseli, layer, mask).
# No proprietary localisation resource, string table or product UI was consulted or copied; add
# entries the same way. Conventions: top-level menus are nouns (Fayil, Gyara, Hoto ...), commands
# are imperatives (Buɗe…, Ajiye a matsayin…), sentence case. Product and technology names
# (PhotoCraft, Photoshop, PSD, OpenType, CMYK, RGB, Lab ...) stay in Latin letters, as do key names,
# units and placeholders; the trailing "…" of dialog commands is kept.
# Hausa plural rule: one|other (one is n = 1; 0 and 2+ take other). Counted nouns follow the noun
# with the number ("fayiloli {n}"); other uses the Hausa plural where one is established, loanwords
# such as layer, pikseli and mask stay unchanged.
# Machine-translated with Claude (Anthropic) for @tronicum; not yet reviewed by a native speaker.
